result.test_isolation_confirmed: Both new tests (http_test.exs:31-63, pollers_test.exs:53-82) call Http.init/1 and Pollers.init(nil) directly, a plain function call per Supervisor.init/2's documented {:ok, {flags, child_specs}} contract -- no Supervisor.start_link, no live process spawned, no port bound. Read lib/letflow/supervisor/http.ex and pollers.ex in full: http_child/0, scheduler_children/0, service_task_dispatcher_children/0 only build child-spec tuples/lists, they never call start_link or open a socket themselves (Bandit/the GenServers are only started if the returned child_specs are subsequently handed to a real Supervisor start, which neither new test does). This confirms TEST-DESIGNER's claim that these two tests avoid ISS-0015's port-collision hazard. Application.put_env mutations are all restored via on_exit/1.

result.verdict_summary: PASS. Independently re-verified all 10 AC-to-test mappings by reading the actual current test code and the fresh requirements.yaml AC text (not the spec file's paraphrase). Both newly-added init/1-direct tests (Http gated-ON, Pollers gated-true child list) are non-vacuous: mutation-tested myself in a throwaway git worktree (mutant applied, test observed to fail with the exact expected assertion diff, then reverted with git checkout -- <path> and confirmed clean via empty git status --porcelain and a re-passing test run) for both. Also ran a supplementary mutation test on AC2's cold-boot ordering test (order-swap in application.ex) given the complexity of that mechanism, confirming genuine discriminating power. AC7's config/ diff independently re-confirmed empty. mix compile clean. Targeted suite passed 72/72 in 2 of 3 runs (1 unreproduced anomaly on the first, uncaptured run, not blocking). No mutant or test artifact left in the working tree -- git status --porcelain is empty in the main repo throughout and after this validation.
